newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip market hounded by weak AT&T shares.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip market hounded by weak AT&T shares.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average fell Wednesday, hit for a second day by the gyrations of powerhouse AT&T Corp. after the telecommunications giant warned that its earnings will disappoint Wall Street.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the 30-stock Dow index was off 5.55 points at 5,868.48. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on moderate volume of 258 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The weakness in the Dow was "a reaction to AT&T opening up and then going down," said James Cramer, president of Cramer Co. "It's so overweighted that ... it is colouring the market more than it should."

AT&T, whose stock if the most widely owned in North America, warned on Tuesday that competition in its key long-distance telephone market would likely result in profit shortfalls for the second half of the year.
The announcement prompted several brokerage houses to downgrade the stock of the telecommunications giant. AT&T was down 1/2 at 51 after tumbling 5-3/4 on Tuesday.

Analysts said the Federal Reserve's decision Tuesday to leave interest rates unchanged meant that the market's preoccupation with monetary policy was likely to continue, with stocks and bonds reacting to every bit of surprising economic data.

"Wall Street loves to worry about something, so it should an erratic market between now and the election, but the bias will be to the upside," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown & Catherwood.
The Fed's decision resolved little in terms of the market's anxieties, said Phil Roth, chief technical analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds.

"We had a knee-jerk favourable reaction to the Fed's non-action on rates and then people said 'Now what?'," he said. "It resolved nothing but the issue of immediate tightening. Now we can worry about later tightening, third quarter earnings or the presidential elections."
Among special situations, the shares of Snyder Communications Inc. jumped more than 20 percent in their initial public offering, climbing 4 to 21 in active trading.
Checkpoint Systems Inc. tumbled 9 to 27-3/8 after the company warned its third quarter results would be below expectations. Apple South Inc. slid 8-1/8 to 12-3/4 also on the company's profit warning.
3Com Corp. rose 6-3/8 to 63 after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 4.08 points at 1,219.35, and the American Stock Exchange index rose 1.12 to 564.52.
